memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Its wick trimmers and trays are to be of pure gold. A talent of pure gold is to be used for the lampstand and all these accessories. See that you make them according to the pattern shown you on the mountain." - Exodus 25:38-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a firm instruction: make everything according to the pattern shown on the mountain. Moses was not free to improve on God's design or adjust it to taste. The tabernacle was to be built God's way, because it represented realities far greater than Moses could see.

That last point matters. Hebrews tells us these things were "a copy and shadow of what is in heaven" (Heb 8:5), which is precisely why the pattern mattered so much. The tabernacle was pointing to something real and eternal — to Christ Himself and the true dwelling of God. Change the copy carelessly, and you distort the picture of the reality.

There is wisdom here for how we approach God today. We are often tempted to reshape faith according to our preferences, keeping the parts we like and quietly adjusting the rest. But God has revealed how we are to come to Him — through Christ alone, on the basis of grace, according to His Word. Our calling is not to redesign the pattern but to receive it gratefully and follow it faithfully. God's ways are not arbitrary restrictions; they are the shape of reality itself, given by the One who sees the whole.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I tempted to reshape faith around my preferences rather than God's Word?
Where do I need to submit to God's pattern instead of my own design?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from reshaping Your truth to suit my preferences. Give me a humble heart that receives Your Word gladly and follows the pattern You have revealed. Amen.
